› Without running any commands or tools, write a 12-line poem about terminal multiplexers.


• At midnight, one dark window splits in two.
  A build runs left; the right waits on a key.
  Below, the logs keep spelling what went wrong;
  Above, a cursor blinks expectantly.
  I name each room so I can find it later,
  Then leave the little engines to their steam.
  Detached, they hum beyond the laptop’s closing,
  Still tending every half-completed scheme.
  By morning, I return and take my place;
  The panes unfold exactly where they were.
  A dozen tasks share one familiar space.
  I stretch my hands. The fans begin to whir.
